title: klient k Daktele: hovory dne, historie čísla, nahrávky
interface: final class Drupal\csobrec\Service\DaktelaClient. Constructor (\GuzzleHttp\ClientInterface $http, \Drupal\Core\Config\ConfigFactoryInterface $configFactory, \Drupal\Core\Site\Settings $settings). The base URL is csobrec.settings:daktela_url with any trailing slash removed; the token is $settings->get('csobrec_daktela_token') and an empty one is \RuntimeException mentioning the token BEFORE any request is sent. THE RULE THAT MUST NOT BREAK: the token travels as the query parameter accessToken (in a header it answers 401), so every request must pass ['query' => …, 'http_errors' => FALSE] and check the status code itself. Guzzle's own exceptions put the full URL — token included — into their message, and that message would end up in the log and in an operator's terminal. Build your own \RuntimeException naming the PATH and the status code, with no previous exception. callsOfDay(\DateTimeImmutable $day, array $queues): array — GET /api/v6/activities.json once PER QUEUE (a query across the whole instance returns thousands of other clients' calls). Query: accessToken, take=1000, skip=0, sort[0][field]=time, sort[0][dir]=asc (the form `sort=time asc` answers 500 to everything), filter[logic]=and and four filters 0..3: type eq CALL, time gte '<Y-m-d> 00:00:00', time lte '<Y-m-d> 23:59:59', queue eq <queue>. Pages: read $body['result']['data'], add skip += 1000 and ask again while the page is full AND fewer rows than $body['result']['total'] have been collected. The merged result is sorted by the 'time' field ascending. No queues means no request. A body that is not JSON, or JSON without 'result', is \RuntimeException. callsOfNumber(string $phone, string $queue): array — the whole history of one number on one queue, no time filter. An empty $queue is \InvalidArgumentException (without a queue the query reaches across the whole instance). Keep only the digits of $phone; it must be at least 9 digits and everything before the last nine must be '', '420' or '00420', otherwise \InvalidArgumentException — 'contains' on a shorter string would match strangers' numbers and we would download a stranger's recording. Neither refusal sends a request. Same paging and sort parameters, filters 0..2: type eq CALL, item.clid contains <last nine digits> (the number is stored in two shapes, so eq misses one; clid and number answer 400), queue eq <queue>. recording(string $activity): ?array — GET /file/recording/<activity> with formats=mp3,ogg,opus,wav and exist=true. The body is either an object {recording,encrypt,format} or a naked JSON false (measured: 18 of 42 calls had no recording). Returns the array, or NULL for a 404 or for a body that is not an array with a non-empty 'recording'. Any other failing status is \RuntimeException — returning NULL there would quietly drop a call out of the batch. download(string $activity, string $target): string — same path with formats only, no exist. Write to a temporary file next to $target and move it into place only after the answer checks out: a failing status, an empty body or a content-type outside audio/* are \RuntimeException, and in every failure case no file — neither $target nor the temporary one — may be left behind (an expired session answers the login page with HTTP 200, and that HTML must never travel to ČSOB as a customer call). On success returns $target, replacing whatever was there.
